 About Choose New Jersey 
 Choose New Jersey is the state’s leading non-profit business attraction organization. We harness the collective power of New Jersey’s business, government, labor, and academic sectors to expand New Jersey’s economy. We work globally, using our marketing expertise, concierge business development services, deep knowledge of the state, and convening power, in collaboration with state government, to empower businesses, entrepreneurs, leaders, and innovators to make New Jersey their home. Learn more at choosenj.com.

 About Kean University 
 Kean University, New Jersey’s urban research university, is a national institution of higher education recognized for its diversity, innovation and the social mobility of its graduates. Designated an R2 research university by the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education, Kean ranks among the top eight percent of U.S. universities for research and doctorate production. Founded in 1855 as a teachers college, Kean has evolved into a thriving research university that supports students as they persist to graduation, give back to their communities and launch successful careers. Kean’s six colleges offer more than 50 undergraduate programs, six doctoral degree programs and more than 70 options leading to master’s degrees, professional diplomas or certifications, across a full range of academic subjects. With campuses in Union, Toms River and Manahawkin, New Jersey, and Wenzhou, China, as well as Kean Online, the University provides students of all backgrounds an affordable and accessible world-class education. Learn more at www.kean.edu . 

 About University of Dubai 
 Established in 1997, the University of Dubai (UD) is an accredited academic institution committed to providing world-class education in the heart of the United Arab Emirates. UD offers undergraduate and graduate programs in business, law, engineering, and information technology through its AACSB- and ABET-accredited colleges. Backed by the Dubai Chamber of Commerce and Industry, the University is recognized for its focus on innovation, research, and strong ties to the public and private sectors. UD plays a vital role in shaping the future workforce of the region and serves as a hub for knowledge exchange, entrepreneurship, and international collaboration.

 About American University in Dubai 
 Founded in 1995 as the first private institution of higher learning in Dubai, AUD is one of the most recognized universities in the UAE – with Ministry of Education licensure and US accreditation (SACSCOC) for the institution, as well as the most prominent US-based professional accreditations for its academic programs: ABET (Engineering), AACSB (Business), NAAB (Architecture), NASAD (Visual Communication and Interior Design), CIDA (Interior Design) and ACEJMC (Communications and Information Studies).

AUD, a university known for its emphasis on effective teaching and the high rate of employability of its graduates, is pleased to be classified as Group II ("Very Good") among research universities according to the UAE Ministry Classification of Higher Education Institutions. AUD has excelled in many areas over the years and has secured the top spot in Student Diversity & Employment Outcomes in Dubai for 2 consecutive years, according to QS Rankings. AUD has also received the "Teaching & Learning Strategy of the Year" award by Times Higher Education MENA 2023. The precedent coupled with AUD's high employability rate (90%+) explains why students from all around the globe with diverse educational backgrounds choose AUD as their destination for higher education.

 About University of Wollongong in Dubai 
 University of Wollongong in Dubai (UOWD) was established in 1993 by one of the world's top-ranking universities - University of Wollongong, Australia. The University of Wollongong in Australia is a modern, research-intensive university with an outstanding reputation for its approach to teaching across a diverse range of academic disciplines. Internationally renowned, University of Wollongong retains a position as one of the top 1% universities in the world, illustrated by its consistent performance in the prestigious QS World University Rankings. UOWD is a branch campus of the University of Wollongong’s international network of learning centres, which deliver the academic excellence of a leading Australian university to strategic locations across the globe.

 About Rowan University 
 Rowan University is ranked among the top 100 public research universities in the United States and is also the third fastest-growing. Known for its innovation in education and dedication to student success, Rowan University offers a wide range of undergraduate and graduate programs designed to meet the needs of the future global workforce.

 American University of Ras Al Khaimah 
 The American University of Ras Al Khaimah (AURAK), located in the United Arab Emirates, is a non-profit, public university that offers a comprehensive set of accredited and internationally recognized undergraduate and postgraduate programs. With a focus on holistic education and practical knowledge, AURAK prepares students to become global citizens who are innovators in their respective fields. Through partnerships with top global universities and organizations, AURAK provides students unparalleled opportunities to gain international exposure and experience.

 This Week in NJ - May 23rd, 2025

 Posted on - 05/23/2025

 Governor Murphy, NJ TRANSIT President & CEO Kris Kolluri Announce Tentative Agreement with Locomotive Engineers Union

 Governor Phil Murphy and NJ TRANSIT President & CEO Kris Kolluri announced a tentative agreement with the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers & Trainmen (BLET), ending the three-day rail stoppage. Regular weekday train service resumed on the start of the service day on Tuesday, May 20, 2025.

“I am pleased to announce that we have reached a fair and fiscally responsible contract settlement that provides a generous wage increase for BLET members while saving taxpayers and customers the burden of fare increases,” said Governor Murphy. “This agreement reflects the commitment of both the BLET and NJ TRANSIT to remain at the table engaging in productive conversations, and I commend them both. Most importantly, it ensures the resumption of rail service for the 100,000 people who depend on our rail system on a daily basis.”

“I am pleased to join Governor Murphy to announce that we have reached a mutually acceptable agreement that is both fair for our locomotive engineers and affordable for our riders and New Jersey taxpayers. I want to thank our customers for their understanding and apologize for any inconvenience during this time, however, it was important to me to reach a deal that didn’t require a significant fare increase,” said NJ TRANSIT President & CEO Kris Kolluri. “I appreciate the BLET leadership’s collaboration at the bargaining table and continuing to negotiate in good faith to get to an agreement. I also want to recognize the thousands of NJ TRANSIT employees who stepped up during this time to support our customers and minimize the impacts to the greatest extent possible.”

 READ MORE 

 Statement by Governor Murphy on House Passage of Disastrous GOP Budget Bill

 Following the House Passage of the GOP Budget Bill, Governor Murphy released the following statement: 

“This bill is a disaster for the American people and the people of New Jersey. By passing this legislation overnight, House Republicans are clearly aware that their extreme, far-right agenda does not reflect the values or priorities of our fellow citizens. 

“In one fell swoop, this bill would rip away health care coverage from struggling families, cut food assistance for our most vulnerable neighbors and children, and raise costs on hardworking Americans.”

“Congressmen Kean, Smith, and Van Drew shamefully voted to approve these devastating cuts and caved on fully repealing the SALT deduction in order to shower billionaires and gun manufacturers with budget-busting tax breaks that will explode our deficit. They have betrayed the people they represent, who will suffer the consequences of their actions.” 

 READ MORE 

 I-80 Eastbound Two Lanes to Reopen in Wharton, Morris County

 Two lanes on I-80 eastbound reopened on Wednesday, May 21 in Wharton, Morris County. 

“Reopening two lanes on I-80 eastbound is a major milestone and the first step in restoring full mobility on this critical interstate highway,” said Governor Phil Murphy. “By the end of next week, two lanes on I-80 westbound are scheduled to be reopened, and all lanes should be reopened by the end of June. I want to commend NJDOT Commissioner Fran O’Connor and the NJDOT crews who have worked tirelessly to make permanent repairs to reopen this highway safely. I also want to thank the New Jersey State Police and the local officials for their partnership in helping manage the traffic diverted to local roadways. And most importantly, we are thanful for the patience of the thousands of New Jerseyans who have been impacted by these sinkholes.”

“We have all been looking forward to this day– the reopening of I-80 eastbound,” NJDOT Commissioner Fran O’Connor said . “I want to thank Governor Murphy, the local elected officials, and the New Jersey State Police for their support and assistance throughout this emergency project, and especially the residents, businesses, and motorists for their patience. None of this would have been possible without the incredible effort of the NJDOT staff and our contractors for working 24 hours a day, 7 days a week for several months to get this highway reopened. The amount of work that has gone into this project is simply astounding. 2 “It is important for motorists to understand a lot of work remains to be done to reopen two lanes on I-80 westbound next week, and all lanes by June 25. I-80 is still an active work zone. For the safety of our workers and motorists, please slow down and obey the reduced speed limits.”

 READ MORE 

 NJEDA Releases Second-Annual Global Economic Index

 The New Jersey Economic Development Authority (NJEDA) presented the 2025 New Jersey Global Economic Index, a report that highlights, ranks, and analyzes the sources of foreign direct investment (FDI) into New Jersey. The annual report, which was first released last year, aims to guide and further develop international business relationships with the state, while bolstering Governor Phil Murphy’s global economic development goals. The report lists 42 countries on the Global Economic Index List, which added five new countries from last year, including Malaysia, Thailand, Romania, Iceland, and Argentina. 

“Throughout my administration, New Jersey has built robust connections with important global partners – from Ireland to the Middle East, and beyond,” said Governor Murphy. “The New Jersey Global Index provides critical insights that sharpen our economic development strategy, enabling New Jersey businesses, agencies, and organizations to seize new global opportunities. This, in turn, will generate jobs, boost the economy, and unlock new opportunities for residents and communities across the state.”

The Global Economic Index indicates that New Jersey, regionally, has the strongest economic relationships with Europe, the Asia Pacific region, and North America. While Europe had the highest number of countries listed as top performers, research found that India ranked first as a global partner with New Jersey, followed by Canada, the United Kingdom, and China. The report notes that the Netherlands, Germany, Switzerland, and Israel also hold a high rank as global partners. Additionally, the Asia-Pacific region is also an area of opportunity for New Jersey, including Japan and South Korea, which ranked ninth and tenth as global partners, respectively.

“This year’s Global Economic Index underscores how far we’ve come in making New Jersey a top-tier destination for international investment,” said NJEDA Chief Executive Officer Tim Sullivan . “Under Governor Murphy’s leadership, New Jersey has deepened its global partnerships and sharpened its focus on high-impact, inclusive growth. This international engagement is essential to attracting new investment, supporting business expansion, and securing the state’s long-term economic competitiveness.”

 Mexico City, Mexico — As part of Governor Phil Murphy’s mission to Mexico City, Choose New Jersey, the state’s leading nonprofit business attraction organization, facilitated a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between New Jersey City University (NJCU) and Fundación Universidad de las Américas Puebla (UDLAP). The agreement, signed by leadership from NJCU and UDLAP and witnessed by Governor Murphy, establishes a framework to strengthen academic and educational collaboration between the institutions.

“New Jersey and Mexico have a unique opportunity to establish a foundation for lasting and shared growth,” said Governor Phil Murphy . “Mexico is New Jersey’s seventh-largest trading partner, and expanding educational opportunities will further strengthen the strong ties between our regions.”

Under the terms of the MOU, the institutions will seek to promote collaboration through student, academic, and administrative exchanges, study abroad programs, double degrees, exchanges of publications and reports, joint research activities, and the organization of academic conferences and seminars, in addition to joint organization of special technical or administrative programs.

“This renewed agreement reaffirms our collective belief that education and economic development are inseparable. Universities are powerful engines of innovation and human capital, and through partnerships like this one, we help shape the talent that drives competitiveness, attracts investment, and fosters social mobility in both Mexico and the United States,” stated Mónica Ruiz Huerta, Vice President of Administration at UDLAP .

"This partnership with Universidad de las Américas Puebla reflects New Jersey City University's commitment to fostering global learning opportunities and cultural exchange," said Andrés Acebo, J.D., President of NJCU . "As New Jersey's oldest Hispanic-Serving Institution, NJCU has a special responsibility to build bridges with leading universities across Latin America. As our campus enters the next era in its nearly 100-year history, partnerships like this exemplify our vision for the future—one that creates meaningful opportunities for academic exchange and enriches both our students and faculty. We're proud to stand with Governor Murphy and Choose New Jersey in expanding the global reach of New Jersey's higher education community."

The agreement was coordinated by the Guarini Institute for International Education & Economic Mobility at NJCU. Drawing on the Institute’s strong track record of global partnerships and economic-mobility programs—including ongoing New Jersey–Mexico initiatives and recent NJCU–UDLAP faculty exchanges—the Guarini Institute, led by Dr. Adrián Franco, Executive Director of the Guarini Institute. will serve as the primary liaison to implement the MOU’s programs.

This partnership comes as NJCU prepares to merge with Kean University to form Kean Jersey City, a transformative initiative tentatively scheduled for completion by July 1, 2026. The collaboration with UDLAP Puebla demonstrates the expanded global reach and enhanced opportunities that will be available to students once the merger is complete.

Also attending the MOU signing will be Kean University President Lamont O. Repollet, Ed.D., and Felice K. Vazquez, Esq. , Chancellor for International Campuses at Kean University, who will sign as a witness to the agreement

“Kean University is proud to stand as a leader in global education, with a campus in China and collaborations spanning Bermuda, Brazil, Dubai, Italy, South Korea, and beyond,” said Kean President Lamont O. Repollet, Ed.D . “Agreements like the one between NJCU and UDLAP expand access to meaningful academic and cultural opportunities for students across institutions. As we move toward establishing Kean Jersey City, international education will remain a top priority, ensuring even more students benefit from immersive cross-cultural experiences.”

“This academic collaboration builds on our efforts to connect New Jersey’s world-class universities with global partners,” said Wesley Mathews, President & CEO of Choose New Jersey . “Partnerships like this create new avenues for academic exchange and demonstrate how higher education can advance economic and cultural ties, promote mutual understanding, and advance long-term development.”

The MOU will remain in effect for three years. The agreement was a highlight of Governor Murphy’s final economic mission with Choose New Jersey, organized in collaboration with the Statewide Hispanic Chamber of Commerce of New Jersey and taking place from November 5-9, 2025.

title: Governor Kathy Hochul
text:
Technology 

 Media 

 Youth 

 Public Safety 

 October 28, 2026 

 Albany, NY

 Video, Audio, Photos & Rush Transcript: Governor Hochul Highlights Efforts to Strengthen Online Youth Safety At Common Sense Media Summit

 Video, Audio, Photos & Rush Transcript: Governor Hochul Highlights Efforts to Strengthen Online Youth Safety At Common Sense Media Summit 

 Governor Hochul: “If we don't listen to our children's cries for help and stand up for protection, then we have failed in one of our most basic, fundamental responsibilities, and failure is not an option. So we took action. We passed legislation protecting children's personal information from being collected and monetized. You're not going to monetize our children's mental health, not here in New York State. Became the first large state in America to literally say — and I was told, ‘Don't do this, Governor. They're going to all hate you’ — we literally took cell phones out of schools and said, ‘No more.’”
 Hochul: “We're protecting not just our children, but the youngest, most vulnerable of all... In New York State, we've stopped companies from sending products to the State of New York that allow this to happen. That there had to be security features. That there had to be notifications. That parents would know that there's a risk involved if you hook up to an internet-enabled baby monitor... When you create a product that can harm people in this state or harm our children, you have to get through me first. So don't go there. Don't go there.”

 Earlier today, Governor Kathy Hochul delivered remarks at the Common Sense Media Summit to highlight her efforts to strengthen AI safety and protect kids online.
 VIDEO : The event is available to stream on YouTube here and TV quality video is available here (h.264, mp4) .
 AUDIO: The Governor's remarks are available in audio form here .
 PHOTOS: The Governor's Flickr page will post photos of the event here. 
 A rush transcript of the Governor's remarks is available below: 
  To all my friends, it is great to see you. And Jim, you just bring such energy and passion to the cause that others will follow. And you had me at hello, I just want to say that, when we first met years ago, and I thought, “This person cares so deeply about just our children and what we can do to protect them from a world that is so vastly different from the one that many of us grew up in, most of us grew up in.”
 And it's happening so quickly, it's almost impossible for parents to know what's going on, for elected officials to stay ahead of it, and we certainly have learned the lesson that we can't count on the companies to put out products that are responsible and that put children first. So we've had to do a lot together, but I so appreciate you and also my friends in the Legislature, especially Senator Kristen Gonzales. And so let's give her a round of applause, and Assemblymember Alex Bores. True champions.
 So we started out the day hearing from young New Yorkers. You've heard them at this conference. They're full of ideas about the future, and it's our responsibility to make sure that as technology transforms their world, that they have every opportunity to grow and to thrive.
 Maybe it comes from being New York's first mom Governor, I’m always thinking about the kids. Always thinking about the kids. But they have to be able to realize their full potential in a safe environment.
 So I want to thank everyone here. We've been working together for such a long time, and none of us are afraid to take on the biggest and most powerful technology companies. Especially here in New York, we're pretty fearless. But we usually win. It's — we're swagger — we have a little bit of swagger here. We like to win.
 But we also want to make sure that it's not just a point of pride for us to be the national leader in protecting children online and hoping that other states will follow. But also, it's just because we care so deeply about people and families. We want them to be safe and protected. So this is, yes we're proud, but we're also just common sense, like all of you, common sense in our approach to doing this. And you have led the step every way.
 This is, as I said, it's deeply personal. I'm hardwired as a mom. I'm actually a grandma, too. Any grandparents? Oh, you all look too young. Grandkids are really good, too. Just wanted to make a plug for those. But we're — hope my kids aren't listening again, they get so annoyed when I do that — but, I started hearing something as I was going around the state as a new Governor. I'd go and do gatherings with young people in school libraries and in conference rooms and in diners. I just thought, “Something's happening. Something deeply troubling is happening to our children.”
 Most of it was the aftermath of the pandemic. This took our kids to such a dark place, and even a couple years ago, it seemed very clear that the adults had gotten over this, right? Okay, that was very bad, but we're going to be okay. We move on. When you think about the kids in their early development years, they don't know that this is going to be their life forever or that it creates this sense of vulnerability: “This could happen to me again next year.” So we have not appreciated what that did to their psyche.
 And also, simultaneous with that was the rise of cell phones in schools, so the kids are addicted to them. And when they're home during this isolation period — many schools did not allow children in for six months, a year — they turn to social media as the crutch, as the replacement, to human interaction, and it's been so hard to pull them back away from that.
 And that's what I'm seeing everywhere. As I sit in these places and gather with them, I talk to them, “What, what has happened?” And some kids would say the pandemic when they were supposed to be able to have their 8th grade graduation or a senior prom, and all the milestones that they were denied. But they're suffering from anxiety and depression at levels we've never seen before, ever before.
 So I started listening to them, and I went out there and what I heard from them was just breaking my heart. And I remember one girl saying — I said, “Why don't you just put down this cell phone?” Because she's saying, “I'm under so much pressure. I have to be listening. I have to watch this to make sure that they're not mocking me about my clothes, they're always teasing about my clothes, or they're all gathering in the girls' restroom right now to talk about what they're doing on the weekend, and I wasn't invited, and they're making plans.” There's — her stress level was off the charts as she's sitting in a library talking to the Governor. She couldn't even focus on me. It's like, it reminded me of when my kids were teenagers, so it wasn't a shock to me.
 But it was just so sad for me to see someone who is so trapped and so addicted. And she said to me, I said, “Why don't you just put the phone down, sweetheart? Why don't you just, can you do this?” She says, “No, but you have to save us from ourselves.” Okay. You're a mom, kid asks you to save them, you're going to step up. You're going to do it. And if we don't listen to our children's cries for help and stand up for protection, then we have failed in one of our most basic, fundamental responsibilities, and failure is not an option.
 So we took action. We passed legislation protecting children's personal information from being collected and monetized. You're not going to monetize our children's mental health, not here in New York State. Became the first large state in America to literally say — and I was told, “Don't do this, Governor. They're going to all hate you” — we literally took cell phones out of schools and said, “No more.”
 Seriously, like everybody from the Education Department to school boards, to principals, to administrators, to parents, to the kids themselves, they said, “Everybody's going to hate you. Don't do this.” I said, “Like I said, done the teenager thing, okay? They usually get over it.” But it was a tough thing to do, but I just could see the right answer: Take it away from them and don't say, “You can, we'll make an exception. You can have it during lunch and study hall.” No. Bell to bell, no.
 And we did that a year ago. A year ago, we announced that, and we had to have all sorts of education. And the parents were very nervous about this, especially with the advent of school shootings, right? They're just like, “I have to be able to connect with my child. I gotta know what's going on in case there's that final message. I need to be able to talk to my baby. I have to.” And when I was able to say, “Law enforcement says, if there is a shooter on the school grounds and around the campus, the last thing you want is for your child's cell phone to start ringing, or they start texting, or they send pictures, or they give a wrong information out to the public or send it to mom, send it to the police. It's the wrong place. So your child is safer when they follow the highly trained individual in the front of the room known as their teacher.”
 So once I got that message out, they started saying, “Aha, maybe it's not safe that my kid's hiding in a closet and their cell phone starts ringing,” right?
 So this is what I had to deal with, but it was so worth it, because despite couple of days, maybe a couple weeks of rockiness, I did a survey from September until May, just this past May, surveying every single school that had done this. Every one was required. Everybody did it.
 What has been the outcome? Teachers were thrilled. They report back that the kids are no longer watching TikTok dance videos all day. They're listening to the math teacher — radical change there — And they're actually talking to each other like human beings. They're bringing board games to lunch. They're playing chess, bingo and cards at lunchtime, and I was so happy. And it said it's really strange for the administration because they walk through the hallways saying, “We hear something we never heard before, children's voices and laughter and shouting.” It was like going into a cemetery. It was dead there. It was so quiet.
 So that's one change that one governor can do to help protect millions of children. But I want every state to do this. Every state has to do this. No state should have a situation where our children are battling and having to fight these forces from social media companies that are trying to pull them into a dark space so they can sell them products and to do all kinds of things and get them addicted for a lifetime.
 It's why people try to promote cigarettes to young teenagers, so they develop those habits, and creating a customer for their entire lives. We also passed a groundbreaking “SAFE Act for Kids”, and sent a message loud and clear to technology companies about what you're able to do with our children's information or not. You cannot touch our children's information. That is protected under the laws of the State of New York.
 And also, we restricted the addictive algorithms from roping our kids in and holding them captive. We know what it's like. I'm seeing all kinds of algorithms. I actually like the Buffalo Bills, so I don't say that much outside of Buffalo, but it's true. Jets and Giants are lovely teams, too. But I get all kinds of feeds showing Josh Allen's latest play because they know I like Josh Allen, right? So I know what they're doing even to me, and I know they're doing that to our kids. So the kids are being hooked on this.
 So what we did — and also, these kids are walking around like zombies. They're not getting enough sleep at night, right? They are not — they're sleep-deprived because they're on their phones all night long. So what we did in New York is we said we're blocking notifications all night long, midnight until 6:00 a.m., to minors without parental consent. And I don't know a single parent who thinks it's good, so they're all going to say no.
 That is now the law of New York. And we set a national standard for age verification. And thanks to advances like this, thank you, we are leading the nation. And that's why I was so proud to be named this year as the number one state in America for protecting, keeping kids safe online. I was very proud to receive that designation.
 [...]
 And last year we were the first state to take on AI chatbots, and we had a bill signed that said there'd be safeguards that direct users to mental health support systems if they engage in conversations about self-harm — that was a step, it was the first time there had been regulations. And remind users that they're talking to a machine, not a human being. And this is, believe it or not, kids are starting to not know the difference, and they're starting to have better relationships with the machines because they're not critical. They try to say the nice things and bring them closer to them. It's really quite horrific what is going on.
 But we have to go further. That was last year. And I want to, again, thank my partners in the Legislature and Common Sense Media for bringing yet another way to enhance the laws we have but make them even better and stronger because we're always playing catch-up, my friends. We're playing catch-up because I don't know when the day is coming when the creators of these products, the AI companies, are going to be responsible in the first place. When they're going to on their own say, “Hey, this could be harmful to kids. Maybe we put safeguards in on the front end. Maybe we have notifications stop during the night.”
 I don't know that I could ever count on that level of social responsibility, but perhaps it comes someday. Perhaps it comes after enough states have legislated. Perhaps it comes if enough lawsuits are filed. But it'd be nice to have that day. But in the meantime, we are going to have to keep leading here legislatively.
 So this morning, you heard from Jim. Just this morning, right before I came here, had my nice Governor's pens and signed two bills: a law that'll safeguard kids from being literally coached by AI chatbots on how to harm themselves. And that is not a hypothetical. That is absolutely what is happening in situations where we have the stories of the moms who came and lobbied us — horrible, horrible stories.
 And also, these machines are creating some sort of illusion and care about them when actually the opposite is occurring. So under our new law, I'm just going to read this to you, no longer will minors have access to chatbots that pretend to be their friends or their boyfriends or girlfriends. They won't [be] able to keep sensitive information about a child's emotional well-being. They'll discourage — no longer can the chatbot discourage people from seeking professional help, and they have done that. They will no longer be able to do that. No longer will they have access to chatbots that can, in any way, encourage thoughts of suicide.
 It's crazy that you have to legislate this. Think about this. It is crazy that we had to sign a bill to stop this. But that shows you how far they've gone, but we've done that. And I want to recognize parents who joined us here today who've had to suffer the unthinkable, and I want them to know that their children's death, as painful as they are, are not in vain. Because of their advocacy, we're going to be able to help stop other families from going through the same trauma and grief that they're experiencing.
 And I want to say this: We're not done, and we did something else this morning too. And I have two little grandkids. When a parent looks at the baby monitor and thinks that this is something keeping their child safe, that they'll know exactly if anything goes wrong, that they don't have to be right in that room, but it turns out that baby monitor — if it's internet-enabled — can literally be spying on their baby or watching a mother nursing her child in that bedroom. That is not hypothetical. That is going on. So once again, we're protecting not just our children, but the youngest, most vulnerable of all.
 So you're a new parent. You're hardwired — every waking moment is to protect that child. So you buy this baby monitor, and it allows you to have freedom a little bit. You can walk in the next hall, you can go to the restroom, throw a load of laundry in. I was the mom who had a baby monitor, not internet-enabled. Didn't have — and I'm not sure the internet was invented back then. We had — I won't talk about that. But, it's just shocking. It's just shocking how bad people are sometimes. To think that there are hackers who are watching you and your baby or watching your child alone.
 One mother said she heard voices in the room, and she walked in, "Where are the voices?" Someone was talking to her baby through the baby monitor. And these despicable criminals are violating this sacred bond between a mother and child when they're together. People have no idea. It's chilling. It's chilling. I want to say this: We've banned that in New York State. In New York State, we've stopped companies from sending products to the State of New York that allow this to happen. That there had to be security features. That there had to be notifications. That parents would know that there's a risk involved if you hook up to an internet-enabled baby monitor.
 So I just want to be clear, I've said a lot today. You have a lot of conference participants to speak and you've had some incredible panels today — I saw all that. We're not against technological change or innovation here in New York. In fact, we have surpassed Silicon Valley and San Francisco for the most number of tech jobs, and I say that with great pride because I'm very competitive. We were number three behind Boston. Then we passed Boston, and now we passed Silicon Valley.
 So I’m just — I'm sorry if you're from California. So people are coming here, the innovators, the young creative talent. We're the number one destination in the country for recent college graduates. So this is the place to innovate. And I don't want any perception that we don't embrace innovation. All we're saying is, when you create a product that can harm people in this state or harm our children, you have to get through me first. So don't go there. Don't go there.
 So we're going to continue working on these issues. Again, I have amazing partners in the Legislature. I want to call them up right now. Assemblymember Alex Bores and Senator Kristen Gonzalez, who have been at my side. I want to thank them for their support. I want to thank all of you for caring enough for our children. That brings you here today, and we're not done yet. So thank you very much, everyone.

title: Governor Kathy Hochul
text:
Economic Development 

 October 21, 2026 

 Albany, NY

 Governor Hochul Announces Ceremonial Groundbreaking for Transformative West Main Gateway Project in Downtown Rochester

 Governor Hochul Announces Ceremonial Groundbreaking for Transformative West Main Gateway Project in Downtown Rochester 

 $5 Million in NYS Support Being Made Available Through the $300 Million Regional Revitalization Partnership Economic Development Strategy — Designed To Build Community Wealth, Foster Small Businesses and Build a Skilled Workforce
 Interactive Map of Projects Advancing Along the West Main Street Corridor 
 Photo of the West Main Gateway Groundbreaking 

 Governor Kathy Hochul today announced a groundbreaking was held for the West Main Gateway Project in the City of Rochester. Administered by OneROC , the project is designed to help revitalize the West Main Street Corridor from West Genesee Street to South Plymouth Avenue, a historically significant but long-underinvested area of Rochester. OneROC will administer the $10 million grant program, funded equally from the Regional Revitalization Program (RRP) and the Ralph C. Wilson Foundation. The fund will provide capital grants for building renovations, small business assistance grants for machinery and equipment, and public realm improvements. The building renovation assistance will provide grant awards for between $25,000 and $250,000 to cover up to 90% of eligible project investments over the next three years.
 “The public-private Regional Revitalization Program initiative is serving as a model for cities across the nation, proving that this type of collaboration is truly a catalyst for transformative economic development,” Governor Hochul said. “By targeting the most underserved neighborhoods in these represented cities, New York State is lifting up and transforming disadvantaged communities, building a more equitable future for all New Yorkers.”
 The groundbreaking took place on West Main Street in front of Rochester Jewels, a nonprofit mentoring organization serving girls in grades 4-12. Extensive roof and window repairs are set to begin at the property ahead of the winter season. The building is one of 22 projects advancing at various stages along the West Main Street corridor. The initiative is also supporting the buildout of a café while additional investment will enhance the façade of the recently re-opened Busy Bee diner. Other supported projects will include work at Morse Lumber, SewGreen Rochester—a nonprofit fiber-arts reuse and education center—along with a local auto shop, arts organization, funeral home, and insurance office.
 Additionally, the Susan B. Anthony Neighborhood Association, Community Design Center of Rochester, and LaBella Associates are helping implement a community-driven planning process for public realm improvements along the corridor. Attendees also got a preview of the emerging vision for public art and amenities in the area as well as forthcoming projects that extend west to the Bull’s Head redevelopment. These projects are expected to leverage more than $3.3 million in additional public and private investment while building momentum throughout the corridor.
 New York State is providing $5 million in support for the project, and the Ralph C. Wilson Foundation has offered another $5 million in capital and other expenses through the RRP -a $300M comprehensive economic development strategy and public-private partnership that maximizes impact and leverages additional investment for Rochester, Buffalo’s East Side, and Niagara Falls.
 The partnership will maximize social and economic impact by co-investing in projects and programs aimed at improving economic conditions to benefit these communities’ residents and businesses. It builds upon and accelerates collaborative, community-driven bodies of work that are already underway. New York has committed $200 million; Ralph C. Wilson, Jr. Foundation, along with other philanthropic and corporate partners committed $80 million; and the remaining $19 million is coming from each city’s local government.

 The combined $80 million for Rochester includes major additional investments in the city’s ongoing waterfront efforts, such as ‘ROC the Riverway’; development of High Falls State Park; further support/expansion of a multi-faceted workforce training programs/facilities; and targets small business assistance along commercial corridors in that city’s most disadvantaged neighborhoods.
 City of Rochester Mayor Malik D. Evans said, “This investment reflects what’s possible when government, philanthropy, businesses, and community organizations come together around a shared vision. We are deeply grateful to Governor Hochul and New York State for their commitment to Rochester and to the West Main Street corridor. These partnerships are essential to moving our city forward, strengthening our neighborhoods, and creating lasting opportunities for Rochester residents and businesses.”
 The ongoing ‘ROC the Riverway’ collaboration with the city is aimed at the revitalization of the Genesee River downtown waterfront. To date, NYS has committed more than $100 million towards dozens of projects, several of which have been completed, including the Brewery Line Trail extension and Pont de Rennes Bridge renovation within the High Falls area. Groundbreaking is planned for later this fall on the 40-acre High Falls State Park in the heart of downtown — the centerpiece of the initiative.
 In December of 2021 , Governor Hochul announced that Rochester was a fifth-round winner of the $10 million Downtown Revitalization Initiative. In December of 2022 , she announced the five projects selected for investment. In May of 2026 , the New York Department of State also announced the completion of the Harper’s Corner project downtown, a $12.8 million mixed-use redevelopment project, supported by the DRI, that transformed four long-distressed commercial buildings into new workforce housing and affordable commercial space.
 Empire State Development President, CEO & Commissioner Hope Knight said, “Dynamic projects like the West Main Gateway transformation demonstrate the importance of the Regional Revitalization Program, led by Governor Hochul and developed with our community partners. The initiative continues to support ideas that will maximize the impact of state investments, bringing new opportunities to marginalized neighborhoods, and serving as a model for inclusive economic growth."
 State Senator Jeremy Cooney said, “The Regional Revitalization Program gives Rochester’s West Main Street Corridor the investment it has long deserved. This initiative supports small businesses, economic growth, and workforce development, creating new opportunities for the entire community. Thank you to Governor Hochul for her continued partnership and commitment to Rochester’s future.”
 Assemblymember Harry Bronson said, “The West Main Gateway Project represents what’s possible when State and private partnerships collaborate with local organizations to bring funding, resources and opportunities to underserved communities. I am proud to have worked with my State Delegation colleagues and Governor Hochul, with the support of Mayor Malik Evans, to secure $10 million in Regional Revitalization Program funds that will connect the historic Susan B. Anthony Museum expansion to the surrounding community to uplift small businesses and neighborhoods through economic development. I also want to extend my gratitude to OneROC and the Ralph C. Wilson Foundation for supporting and sponsoring this transformative opportunity. I look forward to the next phases of the West Main Gateway Project.”
 Assemblymember Demond Meeks said, “These historic investments with public and private funding have the potential for significant impact in Rochester. I want to thank Governor Hochul, Empire State Development, and the Ralph C. Wilson Jr. Foundation for continuing to invest in our community, especially long neglected portions of our city. Revitalizing our downtowns and urban centers will benefit all of New York. Ensuring community-driven planning of development projects is a key component to long-term success. I chose the location of my District Office, in no small part to lead by example and contribute to the surrounding neighborhood. Our friends and neighbors need to know that their leaders are connected to, committed, and invested in the well-being of their neighborhoods and the partners in this project are doing that.”
 Monroe County Executive Adam Bello said, “The West Main Gateway project represents a transformative investment in one of Rochester’s most historic neighborhoods, bringing new energy, new opportunities and new life to a corridor that has long deserved greater attention. By supporting small businesses, revitalizing properties and creating a more vibrant and welcoming streetscape, we are helping build a stronger downtown Rochester for generations to come. The Regional Revitalization Partnership demonstrates the incredible impact we can achieve when government, philanthropy and community partners work together to make meaningful investments in our neighborhoods. Thank you to Governor Kathy Hochul for her continued leadership and unwavering support for Rochester and Monroe County.”
 OneROC President and CEO Joe Stefko said, “Empire State Development, the Ralph C. Wilson Jr. Foundation, and their fellow Regional Revitalization Partnership funders have demonstrated in Buffalo, and, in the Foundation’s case, in Detroit, what becomes possible when public and private partners align around neighborhood investment in flexible and innovative ways. OneROC has led the strategy and coordination required to put that model into action along West Main Street, working closely with the Susan B. Anthony Neighborhood Association and guiding implementation with technical support from LaBella Associates. West Main has an extraordinary history, distinctive architecture, and committed business and property owners. These investments will strengthen the small businesses that make the corridor special and build on the energy and commitment already present throughout the neighborhood. We are grateful to SBANA, our funders and community partners, and the business and property owners investing in West Main Street.”
 Ralph C. Wilson, Jr. Foundation Program Officer Eric Phamdo said, “West Main Street has long been an important part of Rochester’s story, and this groundbreaking is a meaningful step toward its next chapter. We’re proud to support a community-driven effort that invests in local businesses, strengthens the corridor and builds on the energy already growing in the neighborhood.”
 ESL Federal Credit Union Vice President/Director, Community Impact John Paul Perez said, “We’re pleased to celebrate the West Main Gateway groundbreaking and the positive impact this project will have on downtown Rochester’s future. At ESL, our Purpose is to help our community thrive and prosper. By building strong neighborhoods, we can create opportunities for local businesses and residents to flourish. We look forward to witnessing how this project will help business owners invest in their futures while also transforming the corridor into a more welcoming, vibrant destination. We’re proud to support this work alongside partners who are also committed to Rochester’s long-term success.”
 Max and Marian Farash Charitable Foundation CEO Jennie I. Schaff said, “West Main Gateway reflects what’s possible when we invest in the people and places that give Rochester its character. These improvements will build on the neighborhood’s strengths and support the businesses and organizations that bring it to life. We’re proud to be part of this shared commitment to its future.”
 M&T Bank Rochester Regional President Steve Epping said, “At M&T Bank, we believe thriving neighborhoods are built through investment, collaboration and a shared commitment to creating opportunity. The groundbreaking of the West Main Gateway project is an exciting milestone for this corridor and a reflection of the dedication of so many organizations, community leaders and stakeholders. We're proud to support an effort that will strengthen the neighborhood, support local businesses and contribute to Rochester's continued growth for years to come."
 KeyBank Corporate Responsibility Officer, Chiwuike Owunwanne said, “ Revitalization efforts are most successful when they build on a community's existing strengths and create opportunities for residents and local businesses to thrive. The West Main Gateway project reflects that approach, and KeyBank is proud to support the partnerships and investments helping move this corridor forward."
 About the Regional Revitalization Partnership (RRP)

 Governor Hochul Announces Phoenix Tailings to Establish $375 Million Commercial Scale Rare Earth Separation Facility in Monroe County

 Governor Hochul Announces Phoenix Tailings to Establish $375 Million Commercial Scale Rare Earth Separation Facility in Monroe County 

 Cutting-Edge Company Will Occupy 500,000-Square-Foot Location in Eastman Business Park; Commits to Creating At Least 90 New Jobs
 New York State’s $3 Million Investment Helps Rebuild America’s Rare Earth Industrial Base, Promotes Cleaner Production Methods and Boosts National Security
 Photos Available Here 

 Governor Kathy Hochul today announced that Phoenix Tailings, a Massachusetts-based company, has chosen Eastman Business Park in Monroe County for a new $375 million commercial scale, environmentally friendly, rare earth mineral separation facility. The 500,000-square-foot site will process rare earth materials used in products such as electric vehicles, electronics and defense equipment. Most rare earth separation currently takes place in China.
 “I am fully committed to supporting innovative projects and companies that are ready to invest in New York and bring in good-paying jobs,” Governor Hochul said. “Phoenix Tailings will not only create at least 90 new jobs at Eastman Business Park further supporting our state’s innovation economy, but they will also play a critical role in bolstering our national security by building a clean supply chain for rare earth elements in New York, reducing reliance on foreign sources of critical minerals.”
 Phoenix Tailings has developed cutting edge, environmentally friendly processes to recover rare earth metals from mining waste and other industrial sources. The company separates and processes these materials into metals used to make powerful magnets enabling technology to become faster, smaller, stronger and more energy efficient. These metals are also critical components in high-tech defense equipment, medical and healthcare products, advanced manufacturing, smartphones, laptops, electric vehicles and communications systems.
 Rare earth minerals are in high demand because of their use in many everyday products and advanced technologies. China currently processes about 90 percent of the world’s rare earth minerals. Phoenix Tailings is proving that mining waste across the country can provide a crucial domestic source of these highly valued materials, reducing the United States’ dependence on foreign supply chains and environmentally unfriendly foreign production.
 When fully operational, the Rochester facility is expected to separate about 18,000 tons of rare earth material each year, enough to produce about 3,000 tons of rare earth metals at the company’s downstream metallization facilities.
 Phoenix Tailings Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer Nick Myers said, “America and its allies cannot build the next generation of advanced manufacturing on a rare earth supply chain they do not control. Phoenix Tailings is building an innovative, commercial-scale alternative designed to secure the Western supply chain for the rare earth metals that power modern industry — while setting a new standard for responsible production, with zero waste, zero direct process emissions and a safer process for the people who operate it. We are thankful to Governor Hochul and all of our economic development partners for their assistance in making this project happen.”
 New York State, through Empire State Development, is offering Phoenix Tailings up to $3 million in performance-based tax credits through the Excelsior Jobs Tax Credit Program. The company has committed to creating at least 90 jobs. In addition, the project is expected to benefit from broader statutory, local and infrastructure benefits. Greater Rochester Enterprise is also assisting with the project.
 The Rochester facility is expected to eventually support more than 200 direct jobs in New York. Phoenix Tailings plans to begin some operations at Eastman Business Park in 2027, with full production expected in 2028.
 Phoenix Tailings says its separation and metal-making operations are expected to support more than 500 jobs across New York, Massachusetts, New Hampshire and a future site. All told, the company expects to invest $1.2 billion across its U.S. operations.
 The U.S. Department of War’s Office of Strategic Capital has made a conditional commitment of $500 million in long-term loans to help Phoenix Tailings build its rare earth mineral separation system. The commitment was announced in June and is still subject to review before the financing is finalized.
 The U.S. Department of Energy has also awarded the company a $66 million grant. The grant is part of a $147.8 million project to demonstrate how heavy rare earth metals can be produced in the United States from waste materials.
 U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer said, “I’m proud to welcome Phoenix Tailings to the Rochester-Finger Lakes region. This new investment will bring rare earth mineral manufacturing operations, along with at least 90 new, good-paying jobs, to Eastman Business Park. This is critical for reducing our reliance on foreign processors and protecting our national security. I’ve long championed Eastman Business Park as a hub for manufacturing and am glad that new companies are recognizing what I have long known: Upstate New York is a prime destination for new manufacturing investments. I am grateful for Governor Hochul’s partnership welcoming new investments to the state.”
 U.S. Senator Kirstin Gillibrand said, “When New York State invests in trailblazing industrial projects such as this new Phoenix Tailings facility, it is imperative that the surrounding communities be able to reap the rewards. With millions in federal investment, this facility will be more than just a new building — it will create jobs for hard-working New Yorkers, contribute to a culture of environmental consciousness, and revolutionize our national security supply chains.”
 Representative Joe Morelle said, “America's dependence on foreign countries for the critical minerals and rare earths that power our economy and our national defense is a vulnerability we cannot afford. Phoenix Tailings’ $375 million investment will put our region to work rebuilding America’s critical mineral supply chain, transforming waste into the materials that enable everything from wind turbines to advanced fighter jets. This is about making sure the next generation of American innovation is built right here in Rochester, by American workers. I’m proud to welcome Phoenix Tailings to Rochester, and I thank Governor Hochul and our local partners for helping make this investment possible.”
 The reinvigorated Eastman Business Park , where Kodak began making photographic film and paper more than a century ago, is a priority for the Finger Lakes Regional Economic Development Council. Today, Eastman Business Park hosts more than 100 companies that collectively employ over 6,000 people.
 Empire State Development President, CEO and Commissioner Hope Knight said, “Under Governor Hochul’s leadership, New York State continues to partner with innovative, dynamic companies that want to invest, grow and create jobs. Phoenix Tailings’ commitment means that new high-tech jobs and advanced technologies will be coming to Eastman Business Park, supporting regional economic growth in the Finger Lakes and demonstrating the success of our strategic efforts.”
 State Senator Jeremy Cooney said, “I’m pleased to see this investment in Monroe County, bringing high-quality jobs to the region, stimulating economic growth, and strengthening local supply chains. These kinds of projects are exactly what our community needs, and I’m proud to see Eastman Business Park continue to attract innovative companies and new opportunities. Thank you to Governor Hochul for continuing to support innovation and opportunity across Greater Rochester.”
 Assemblymember Sarah Clark said, “Eastman Business Park has an incredible history of supporting innovation and good jobs in Rochester, and today's announcement from Phoenix Tailings shows how that legacy can continue to grow. Rochester has long been a leader in manufacturing, finding new uses for existing materials and building a stronger circular economy. This project for a rare earth mineral separation facility using industrial waste streams will build on Rochester's tradition of creating cutting edge jobs, attracting new investment, and demonstrating how innovation can continue to drive our city forward. I am grateful for everyone who has worked to make this project a reality and look forward to seeing the economic impact that it has on our community.”
 Monroe County Executive Adam Bello said, “We are proud to welcome Phoenix Tailings to Monroe County and thrilled that they have chosen Eastman Business Park for this significant investment in our community. Their innovative technology is transforming industrial waste into critical materials that power everything from electric vehicles to advanced manufacturing, strengthening American supply chains and creating new opportunities for economic growth. With a $375 million investment and the promise of hundreds of new jobs, Phoenix Tailings is helping build the next generation of advanced manufacturing right here in Monroe County. Thank you to Governor Kathy Hochul for her leadership and unwavering support for our community, and for her continued commitment to bringing good-paying jobs and new opportunities to our region.”
 Greece Town Supervisor Jeff McCann said, “Just as Kodak Park was an integral part of Greece's growth and development, so too is Eastman Business Park's success tied to Greece's future. The addition of Phoenix Tailings and its 90 new jobs will not only help Greece's economy, it will cement Eastman Business Park's role as a hub for advanced manufacturing in our region. We are grateful to Governor Hochul and Commissioner Knight for supporting the upstate economy by bringing this major project to our community.”
 City of Rochester Mayor Malik D. Evans said, “I want to welcome Phoenix Tailings to the Rochester community and thank them for making this tremendous investment in our region, which will strengthen our position as an advanced manufacturing hub and create good-paying jobs for our residents. Thank you as well to Governor Kathy Hochul, Empire State Development and all of our partners who supported this project for working together to accelerate the growth of Rochester’s innovation economy."
 Greater Rochester Chamber of Commerce President and Finger Lakes Regional Economic Development Council Co-Chair CEO Bob Duffy said, “Congratulations to Nick Myers and the whole Phoenix Tailings team on this tremendous announcement! With the opportunity to grow anywhere, this investment in Greater Rochester, and specifically in Eastman Business Park, is a strong signal that our community is open for business, capitalizing on our historic legacy to propel future growth and innovative redevelopment. Eastman Business Park is growing into a hub for job creation, sustainability, and once again, regional pride. Thank you to Governor Kathy Hochul, Nick Myers and all other partners whose leadership contributed to this decision. We are proud to help welcome Phoenix Tailings to our community.”
 Greater Rochester Enterprise President Matt Hurlbutt said, “We are pleased that Phoenix Tailings found the right site, infrastructure, and skilled workforce to support its rare earth separation facility in the Greater Rochester, NY region. GRE worked with Phoenix Tailings on every aspect of this project, from site selection and incentives to permitting and talent. We’ll continue to support the company’s leadership team as they expand their operations in the Greater Rochester, NY, region.”
 For additional information about Phoenix Tailings, visit phoenixtailings.com .
 Accelerating Economic Development in the Finger Lakes 
 Today’s announcement complements “Finger Lakes Forward,” the region’s comprehensive strategy to generate robust economic growth and community development. The regionally designed plan focuses on investing in key industries including photonics, agriculture‎ and food production, and advanced manufacturing. More information is available here .

 Governor Hochul Announces Completion of Barrel Factory Apartments, Bringing 100 New Homes to Kingston

 Governor Hochul Announces Completion of Barrel Factory Apartments, Bringing 100 New Homes to Kingston 

 100-Unit Mixed-Use, Mixed-Income Development Adds 80 Market-Rate and 20 Affordable Homes in Midtown Kingston
 New York State Supported Barrel Factory Complex With $5.62 Million in Funding

 Governor Kathy Hochul today announced the completion of Barrel Factory Apartments, a $24 million mixed-use, mixed-income development at 110 Cornell Street in Midtown Kingston. Supported by a $4.78 million Mid-Hudson Momentum Fund grant from Empire State Development, the four-story building adds 100 new homes, including 20 affordable to households earning up to 80 percent of the Area Median Income, along with street-level retail on Cornell Street. The project is the second phase of the Barrel Factory Complex, a community-focused redevelopment by MHV Development that is transforming formerly vacant and underutilized properties into a new residential and commercial hub in Midtown Kingston.
 “Today we are marking the completion of 100 new homes in Midtown Kingston, including 20 affordable apartments, alongside new commercial space and the continued redevelopment of the historic Barrel Factory site,” Governor Hochul said. “New York’s investment through the Mid-Hudson Momentum Fund helped advance this mixed-use development and expand the housing supply in the heart of Kingston, while building on the work already underway to bring long-vacant properties back into productive use.”
 Empire State Development President, CEO and Commissioner Hope Knight said, “Barrel Factory Apartments brings together new housing, commercial activity and the productive reuse of long-vacant properties in one coordinated redevelopment. ESD’s Mid-Hudson Momentum Fund investment helped move this second phase forward, adding 100 homes in Kingston while creating new space for businesses and makers and building on the successful restoration of the historic Barrel Factory.”
 Developed by MHV Development, Barrel Factory Apartments includes 80 market-rate and 20 affordable homes, street-level commercial space and the restoration of The Barn at the Barrel Factory, an approximately 21,000 square foot former warehouse that is now leased to Free to Thrift and other professional and maker uses. The Barn has the potential to support up to 20 jobs and, together with new retail space, will help bring additional activity to the Cornell Street corridor.
 MHV Development Partner Danny Sirotkin said, “MHV Development is incredibly grateful to Governor Hochul and Empire State Development for the Mid-Hudson Momentum Fund award, which has been instrumental in bringing the Barrel Factory Apartments to life. We also want to thank the City of Kingston for their partnership and shared vision in transforming this underused site into a mixed-use community with 100 new apartments.”
 The project builds on the first phase of the Barrel Factory Complex, a $4.6 million adaptive reuse of the historic 120-year-old Kingston Barrel Factory, which had been vacant for approximately 15 years. Supported by an $840,000 Restore New York Communities Initiative grant, Phase I created 12 affordable apartments, approximately 3,500 square feet of commercial flex space and shared amenities. Together, the two phases have created 112 homes — including 32 affordable units — while adding new commercial space and returning long-underutilized properties to productive use in Midtown Kingston.
 Mid-Hudson Regional Economic Development Council Co-Chairs Dr. Marsha Gordon and Dr. Kristine Young said, “The Barrel Factory Complex is bringing much-needed housing, new commercial activity and space for local businesses to Midtown Kingston, while transforming long-underutilized properties into a vibrant mixed-use destination. This project will strengthen the neighborhood, support continued economic growth and create new opportunities for residents and businesses. We thank Governor Hochul for her continued investment in the Mid-Hudson region.”
 In addition to the funding from New York State, the Community Preservation Corporation, a New York-based nonprofit multifamily finance company, provided $19.5 million in construction financing as well as $16.3 million in Freddie Mac permanent financing to support the project.
 Community Preservation Corporation Chief Business Officer and Head of Community Preservation Corporation Capital Nicole Ferreira said, "The Barrel Factory Apartments are a powerful example of how thoughtful redevelopment can breathe new life into historic properties while creating housing that communities need today. CPC is proud to partner with MHV Development, Governor Hochul, Empire State Development, and our local partners to help transform this long-vacant site into a vibrant mixed-use destination that honors Kingston's history, expands housing opportunities, and contributes to the continued revitalization of Midtown."
 Ulster County Executive Jen Metzger said, “Seeing the Kingston Barrel Factory and the entire mixed‑use development fully completed is an incredible moment for Midtown Kingston. What was once a long‑abandoned historic property has now been transformed into affordable live/work space, commercial storefronts, and a new 100‑unit mixed‑income building that will bring housing, jobs, and creative energy to this neighborhood. This project shows what is possible when we invest in our communities, honor our history, and build a stronger future for our residents. I want to thank Governor Hochul, Empire State Development, MHV Development, Mayor Noble, and the Restore NY and Momentum Fund programs for helping make this transformative project a reality.”
 City of Kingston Mayor Steve Noble said, “The Barrel Factory is a great example of how we can transform underutilized properties into places that strengthen our community, creating much-needed housing while bringing new opportunities for local businesses. These 100 new homes are an important addition to Kingston and will help bring new energy and continued investment to Midtown. I want to thank Governor Hochul and Empire State Development for their continued partnership."
 State Senator Michelle Hinchey said, "The Barrel Factory development is a great model for mixed-income, mixed-use housing. It takes our disused industrial space and revitalizes it to housing and commercial space for the residents of Kingston. I'm proud to have fought for State budget funding for the project and of the work of our local and State partners who brought non-profits, developers, and government together to make this happen. I especially want to thank and congratulate Governor Hochul, MHV Development and the Mid Hudson Momentum Fund for their work and support on this project.”

 Governor Hochul Celebrates Completion of IMA Life North America’s $30 Million Expansion Project in Tonawanda 

 New 120,000-Square Foot Facility Will Support Company’s Production of State-of-the-Art Pharmaceutical Equipment — Including Equipment for Cancer-Fighting Treatments
 Expansion Allows the Company To Create 70 New Jobs and Retain 195 Jobs in Western New York
 See Photos of the Completed Project 

 Governor Kathy Hochul today announced that manufacturing company IMA Life North America has completed its $30 million, 120,000-square-foot facility in Tonawanda to increase its production of freeze-drying equipment for the pharmaceutical industry. IMA Life's equipment is shipped all over the world and its customers include pharmaceutical giants such as Pfizer and Moderna.
 “The expansion of IMA Life’s Tonawanda facility advances New York's leadership in medical manufacturing by providing essential equipment for life-saving treatments and creating high-quality regional jobs,” Governor Hochul said. “The completed project reinforces the state's ability to attract premier investments and talent, securing Western New York’s role in the global pharmaceutical supply chain.”
 IMA Life North America is part of IMA Group, an Italian company that is a global leader in the field of aseptic drug processing and freeze-drying equipment, with about 7,400 employees worldwide. The company offers a wide range of technologically advanced machines, which preserve the integrity of pharmaceutical products, ensuring the maximum level of sterility and protecting both the operator and the environment.
 The new building includes 90,000 square feet of production space and 30,000 square feet of office space on a 15-acre parcel located at 700 Colvin Woods Parkway, replacing IMA Life’s existing 60,000-square-foot facility at 2175 Military Road.
 The large freeze dryers manufactured there can rapidly convert vials of liquid medicines and other pharmaceutical products into a powdered form that is shelf-stable and easy to transport. The product range includes blowers, washers, depyrogenation tunnels, liquid and powder fillers, freeze dryers, automatic loaders/unloaders, labelers and isolation systems.
 IMA Life North America President Ernesto Renzi said, “IMA Life offers a broad range of technologically advanced machines, which preserve the integrity of pharmaceutical products, ensuring the maximum level of sterility and protecting both the operator and the environment. IMA Life's equipment is shipped all over the world and its customers include the main multinational companies in the industry.”
 IMA Life has 195 employees based in Tonawanda and is actively adding 70 more personnel as the newly opened expansion project unlocks production increases. New York State, through Empire State Development (ESD), the State’s economic development agency, will provide up to $1.1 million in performance-based Excelsior Jobs Program tax credits in return for IMA’s job creation commitments.
 Empire State Development President, CEO and Commissioner Hope Knight said, “The completion of IMA Life’s expansion cements Upstate New York as a premier hub for advanced pharmaceutical manufacturing. By delivering on this state-of-the-art facility, we are leveraging our highly skilled workforce and strategic partnerships to drive economic growth and secure Western New York’s position on the global stage.”
 Montante Construction President Doug Elia said, “Helping great companies grow in Western New York is at the heart of what we do at Montante. We are grateful to IMA Life for their partnership and confidence in Montante Construction, and I am incredibly proud of our employees, trade partners and project team whose dedication and expertise made this complex project a success while helping ensure IMA's continued growth and investment in Tonawanda.”
 New York State Health Commissioner Dr. James McDonald said, “I thank Governor Hochul for her continued commitment to supporting good jobs across New York and strengthening our communities. Medication represents hope for patients and their loved ones. IMA Life’s investment will help support that work while creating new employment opportunities for New Yorkers.”
 State Senator Jeremy J. Zellner said, “This is exactly the kind of investment we want to see in Western New York. A company choosing Tonawanda, creating 70 new jobs and putting down deeper roots in our community. What makes this especially significant is that the work being done here reaches far beyond Western New York. The equipment built by workers in Tonawanda plays a role in producing medicines and treatments used around the world. I’m proud to welcome this next chapter for IMA Life and grateful to Governor Hochul for helping make this continued growth possible.”
 Assemblymember William Conrad said, “The construction of this facility signifies another major boost to Tonawanda's long and well-earned reputation as a hub for industry. The business community we have in Colvin Woods sits at the cutting edge of manufacturing, fabrication and engineering; in other words, this is a center for the best and brightest our region has to offer. It's a celebratory day when we as a collective, and with Empire State Development's keen direction, can facilitate the growth of a Colvin Woods partner like IMA Life. A company known for setting the standards for aseptic processing and freeze-drying, IMA Life is forever exploring the technology of the future, the applications of which seem limitless. This is another corporate entity we can be immensely proud of, from the Town of Tonawanda and beyond.”
 Erie County Executive Mark C. Poloncarz said, “Erie County is the proud home of IMA Life's North America headquarters. We are thrilled to see the significant growth and new job creation in our community from a large, diverse global company. As a board member of the Erie County Industrial Development Agency, I gladly supported all phases of this project, and the $5.1 million in IDA incentives will pay dividends for years to come. Once again, another global manufacturer has shown that Erie County can compete with anywhere.”
 Town of Tonawanda Supervisor John Flynn said, “The Town of Tonawanda is incredibly proud to celebrate the completion of IMA Life’s state-of-the-art facility at Colvin Woods Parkway. I thank Governor Hochul and ESD for supporting this $30 million investment that not only retains nearly 200 high-quality positions in our community but opens the door for 70 new, forward-thinking jobs. IMA Life's commitment to our town reinforces Tonawanda’s standing as a prime location for innovative global companies to plant roots, expand and thrive.”
 About IMA Life North America 
 IMA Life North America is one of six IMA Life production sites. IMA Life is part of IMA Group, a world leader in the design and manufacture of automatic machines for the processing and packaging of pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, food, tea and coffee, as well as in automation solutions. IMA Life, which includes the production sites of IMA Life North America, IMA Life Calenzano, IMA Life PharmaSiena, IMA Life Beijing and IMA Life Shanghai, offers a comprehensive product portfolio to process liquids and powders in aseptic and non-aseptic environments. Its offering includes vial and ampoule washers, depyrogenation tunnels, decontamination technologies, filling and closing machines for ampoules, Ready-To-Use vials, syringes and pre-capped cartridges for medium and high-speed production. The portfolio also encompasses gloveless technologies for ATMPs, Cell & Gene therapies and radiopharmaceuticals, as well as powder microdosing and macrodosing systems, capping machines and a full range of containment solutions, including Restricted Access Barrier Systems and isolators, further strengthened by IMA ProSys technologies for containment and isolator systems.
 IMA Life also offers lyophilisation process development and continuous aseptic spray freeze drying technology, together with industrial, pilot and laboratory freeze dryers and automatic or semi automatic vial loading and unloading systems for freeze dryers. The range is completed by assembly and labelling machines for syringes, and labelling machines for vials, ampoules, shaped containers, pre-filled pens, Blow Fill Seal single dose containers and cartons with the latest serialization technologies. Blowing machines, depackers, tray loaders and other ancillary equipment further enhance the portfolio, ensuring truly comprehensive coverage of pharmaceutical processing and packaging needs.
 For more information, visit: www.imagroup.com and www.imagroup.com/pharma
